adventure.title: Ride La Grande Roue at the Old Port
adventure.description: Sixty metres over the St. Lawrence in a climate-controlled cabin — the wheel turns year-round and the skyline does the rest.
adventure.bonus: Go at golden hour and don't take a single photo.

adventure.title: Lap the Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve by Bike
adventure.description: When the F1 circus is away the Grand Prix track belongs to anyone on two wheels — roll onto Île Notre-Dame and take the Senna corner at your own top speed.
adventure.bonus: Time your fastest lap and report it to a friend like it matters.

adventure.title: Climb the Tour de Lévis on Île Sainte-Hélène
adventure.description: A 1930s stone tower hides in plain sight at Parc Jean-Drapeau — climb the spiral stairs for a 360° river-and-skyline view most Montrealers have never seen.
adventure.bonus: Count the steps on the way up — commit to a guess before you check.

adventure.title: Bike the Plateau's Ruelles Vertes
adventure.description: Montreal's ruelle network in the Plateau is a secret city of murals, gardens, and cats that only locals actually use.
adventure.bonus: Find a mural you've never seen documented online and photograph it before moving on.

adventure.title: Rooftop Plunge at Bota Bota Spa
adventure.description: This converted river ferry moored in the Old Port runs a Nordic circuit — steam, cold plunge, rest — with the St. Lawrence lapping the hull below you.
adventure.bonus: Do three full hot-cold cycles and stay in the cold pool for a full minute each time.

adventure.title: Explore the Underground City (RÉSO)
adventure.description: Thirty-three kilometres of tunnels connect metro stations, malls, and office towers — a parallel city that Montrealers treat as a winter survival reflex.
adventure.bonus: Navigate from McGill station to Place des Arts using only underground corridors — no phone maps allowed.

adventure.title: Climb Mont Royal at Dawn
adventure.description: The city spreads out below you in silence as the sun cracks the skyline from the Kondiaronk Belvedere.
adventure.bonus: Ditch the main trail and bushwhack up the steep east face through the woods.

adventure.title: Kayak the St. Lawrence near Habitat 67
adventure.description: Launch a kayak into the current beside Moshe Safdie's iconic housing complex and the downtown skyline.
adventure.bonus: Paddle close enough to touch Habitat 67's concrete cubes from the water.

adventure.title: Bike the Lachine Canal to the Old Port
adventure.description: Pedal the flat waterside path from Atwater Market all the way to the cobblestones of the Old Port.
adventure.bonus: Stop at one lock and watch a boat pass through.

adventure.title: Jet-Boat the Lachine Rapids
adventure.description: Get drenched blasting through the St. Lawrence's whitewater on a Saute-Moutons jet boat, minutes from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Sit in the very front row and take the full soak.

active.title: Cross-Country Ski Parc du Mont-Royal
active.description: When the snow holds, the groomed loops through the mountain's hardwood forest are a 20-minute bus ride from downtown and feel like a different country entirely.
active.bonus: Ski the full outer perimeter loop without consulting your phone once — use the trail markers only.

active.title: Pick-Up Hockey at Patinoire Laurier
active.description: Show up at Parc Laurier's outdoor rink on any winter weekend and you'll find the kind of honest pick-up hockey that Montreal has been playing in its parks for over a century.
active.bonus: Score a goal and do a full-ice lap celebration without apologizing for it.

active.title: Climb at Allez Up
active.description: Saint-Henri's cathedral-sized climbing gym with towering lead walls and a committed local scene makes any weeknight feel like a proper athletic event.
active.bonus: Project a route one grade above your limit and don't leave until you've sent it clean.

active.title: Run the Lachine Rapids Trail
active.description: The gravel path hugging the St. Lawrence from LaSalle to Parc des Rapides puts roaring whitewater on your right and herons wading in the shallows on your left for a 10 km out-and-back.
active.bonus: Hit the turnaround point at the rapids overlook, strip off your shirt, and let the mist hit you before heading back.

active.title: Swim at Bain Morgan
active.description: This restored 1930s public baths in Hochelaga-Maisonneuve turns a lap swim into a time-travel experience inside one of Montreal's grandest neighbourhood institutions.
active.bonus: Do the full 1,500 m without stopping and reward yourself with a coffee at the corner dep on the way out.

active.title: Skate the Atwater to Bassin Peel Stretch
active.description: The inline skating path running from Marché Atwater along the Lachine Canal to Bassin Peel is a flat, fast, two-kilometer groove that the city built specifically for going hard.
active.bonus: Complete the full out-and-back without stopping — no walking sections allowed.

active.title: Early Morning Swim at Plage de l'Île Notre-Dame
active.description: Montreal's urban beach on Île Notre-Dame opens at 10am with filtered St. Lawrence water, sandy shores, and a crowd that actually swims instead of just posing.
active.bonus: Swim to the far buoy line and back without stopping — no floating allowed.

active.title: Sprint Intervals on the Mount Royal Running Loop
active.description: The 5.5-kilometre perimeter trail around the mountain is the unofficial training ground of Montreal's endurance running community — everyone is faster here than they should be.
active.bonus: Race the next person who passes you — if they accept, you both go all out to the next lamppost.

active.title: Paddleboard at Parc Jean-Drapeau Beach
active.description: Balance across the calm, filtered swimming beach on an island built for a World's Fair.
active.bonus: Paddle out past the buoy line and back before resting.

active.title: Skate the Old Port Rink at Bonsecours Basin
active.description: Glide across a lit outdoor rink on the waterfront with the Old Port's stone buildings glowing behind you.
active.bonus: Skate one full lap without holding the boards.

active.title: Pedal-Boat on Beaver Lake
active.description: Paddle a rented boat across Mount Royal's small mountaintop lake, skyline peeking through the trees.
active.bonus: Race the boat next to you to the far shore.

social.title: Sunday Afternoon at Sala Rossa
social.description: Sala Rossa is Mile End's most charming event hall — any given Sunday could mean a record fair, a film screening, or a world-music show you didn't expect to love.
social.bonus: Introduce yourself to whoever's next to you and find out what brought them here today.

social.title: Friday Night at Quai des Brumes
social.description: This Mile End bar has been the city's literary-bohemian living room since 1987 — come for a Boréale and stay until you've argued about something that matters.
social.bonus: Order in French the entire night — no switching to English no matter how easy it would be.

social.title: Underground Show at L'Esco
social.description: L'Escogriffe is the archetypal Montreal dive venue — tight room, cheap beer, local bands who actually rip — and it's been doing it since 1993.
social.bonus: Get to the front rail before the headliner starts and hold your position for the whole set.

social.title: Dinner at Maison Boulud
social.description: Scoring a counter seat at the Ritz-Carlton's formal Montreal outpost means watching Daniel Boulud's kitchen operate at full precision from two feet away while eating one of the city's most technically demanding tasting menus.
social.bonus: Ask the chef de partie directly what dish they're most proud of tonight and order it regardless of what you planned.

social.title: Late Night at Casa del Popolo
social.description: This Mile End institution has hosted the city's most important underground music and literary nights since 2001, with a back room that still somehow feels like a discovery.
social.bonus: Buy a drink for whoever is performing or running the event and tell them exactly what you thought.

social.title: Afternoon Pint at Dieu du Ciel!
social.description: The Plateau's legendary craft brewery has been pouring boundary-pushing beers from its narrow room on Laurier since 1998, with a rotating tap list that regulars plan their weeks around.
social.bonus: Ask the bartender what's on cask right now and order that instead of whatever you had in mind.

social.title: Terrasse Dîner at Fabergé
social.description: The long sun-soaked terrasse on Bernard in Outremont is where the neighbourhood actually eats — good wine, shareable plates, and the kind of slow Tuesday lunch that feels stolen from another life.
social.bonus: Order a bottle of something you can't pronounce and split the whole thing before the cheque arrives.

social.title: Saturday Night at Bar Le Ritz PDB
social.description: The Plateau's beloved dive-turned-concert venue runs a tight room where sweaty indie shows and cheap tallboys have been the formula since the neighbourhood was still rough around the edges.
social.bonus: Get to the front of the room before the headliner starts and stay there the whole set.

social.title: Afternoon at Marché Atwater
social.description: Montreal's most beautiful market pulls you in with butchers, fromageries, and flower stalls under a soaring Art Deco tower that's anchored the Saint-Henri waterfront since 1933.
social.bonus: Buy one unpasteurized Quebec cheese you've never heard of and eat it on the canal bench before you leave.

social.title: Catch a Canadiens Game at Bell Centre
social.description: Feel the loudest arena in the NHL erupt for the most storied franchise in hockey history.
social.bonus: Learn to sing along to 'Ole Ole Ole' before puck drop.

social.title: Bar-Hop Mile End's Cocktail Scene
social.description: Weave through Mile End's speakeasies and natural wine bars, Montreal's most stylish few square blocks.
social.bonus: Let the bartender build you something off-menu at every stop.

social.title: Join the Tam-Tams Drum Circle
social.description: Spend a Sunday at the foot of Mount Royal's monument where hundreds gather to drum, dance, and picnic.
social.bonus: Bring or borrow a drum and actually join in.

social.title: Catch a Set at Upstairs Jazz Bar & Grill
social.description: Duck into this basement jazz institution for a live set and a plate of something Cajun-inflected.
social.bonus: Sit at the bar closest to the stage instead of a table in back.

chill.title: Explore the Redpath Museum
chill.description: McGill's 1882 natural history cabinet — dinosaur bones, Egyptian mummies, and taxonomy drawers — is genuinely one of North America's most underrated museum rooms.
chill.bonus: Find the case with the specimen that disturbs you most and stay in front of it for a full two minutes.

chill.title: Dinner at Le Vin Papillon
chill.description: Joe Beef's wine bar sibling on Notre-Dame Ouest serves vegetable-forward plates and an unhinged natural wine list in a room so small and precise it feels like eating at a chef's private party.
chill.bonus: Tell the server you want no menu — just let the kitchen send whatever they feel like tonight, and say yes to every wine pairing.

chill.title: Sunday Reading at Café Cherrier
chill.description: The grande dame of Plateau terrasses has anchored the corner of Cherrier and Saint-Denis since 1983 — a Bloody Mary, a newspaper, and three hours with nowhere to be.
chill.bonus: Leave your phone in your pocket for the entire visit — order, eat, read, and people-watch without unlocking it once.

chill.title: Chill at Cinéma Sous les Étoiles
chill.description: Parc Jarry's summer outdoor cinema screens cult films and Québécois classics on a massive inflatable screen while you're flat on your back in the grass with a beer in hand.
chill.bonus: Arrive early enough to claim a spot dead-centre and talk to the person next to you before the film starts.

chill.title: Sunset on the Jacques Cartier Bridge Lookout
chill.description: The pedestrian path on the Jacques-Cartier Bridge delivers an unobstructed panorama of the St. Lawrence, the islands, and downtown going gold at dusk.
chill.bonus: Stop at the exact center of the bridge and stay there for five full minutes watching the water below.

chill.title: Spend an Hour at the Musée des Beaux-Arts
chill.description: The MBAM's permanent collection spans Inuit carvings to European masters and the building itself — five connected pavilions — is worth the walk-through alone.
chill.bonus: Pick one piece, sit in front of it for ten uninterrupted minutes, and form one real opinion about it.

chill.title: Sit in on a Show at Église Saint-Jean-Baptiste
chill.description: One of Montreal's grandest 19th-century churches hosts intimate classical and choral concerts where the acoustics do things that concert halls can't.
chill.bonus: Sit in the first three rows and close your eyes for an entire movement.

chill.title: Browse Librairie Drawn & Quarterly
chill.description: This Mile End indie bookshop is the spiritual hub of Montreal's literary and comics scene — unhurried, beautifully curated, no hustle required.
chill.bonus: Buy one book chosen entirely by the staff recommendation shelf without reading the back cover.

chill.title: Afternoon in Parc La Fontaine
chill.description: Plateau's sprawling urban park delivers paddle boats on the pond, shaded benches, and the unhurried energy of a city that genuinely knows how to be outside.
chill.bonus: Rent a pedal boat and navigate to the center of the pond — no hands on the wheel for 60 seconds.

chill.title: Read on the Terrasse at Café Olimpico
chill.description: The Mile End espresso landmark pours the same doppio it's been pulling since 1970 and the sidewalk terrace on St-Viateur is the best free seat in the neighbourhood.
chill.bonus: Strike up a conversation with whoever's been there longest — they have stories.

chill.title: Wander the Montreal Botanical Garden
chill.description: Lose an afternoon in ten themed gardens, from a Chinese lantern courtyard to a First Nations garden.
chill.bonus: Find the Japanese garden and sit there for ten full minutes.

chill.title: Sunset Picnic on Mount Royal
chill.description: Climb to the lookout at Parc du Mont-Royal and watch the whole city glow gold, then blue, then lit.
chill.bonus: Stay until the city lights fully switch on below you.

chill.title: Sit with the Silence at Notre-Dame Basilica
chill.description: Step into the deep blue, gold-starred interior of one of the most stunning basilicas in North America.
chill.bonus: Sit in a different pew than you normally would and just look up.

chill.title: Stroll the Old Port Waterfront
chill.description: Wander cobblestone streets and the river promenade where Montreal's history and its waterfront meet.
chill.bonus: Walk to the very end of the clock tower pier and back.

foodie.title: Dim Sum at Maison Kam Fung
foodie.description: Cart service, enormous dining room, and dumplings that have been pulling Chinatown families in since 1980 — this is the real Sunday ritual.
foodie.bonus: Flag down every cart that passes and say yes to anything you can't immediately identify.

foodie.title: Tacos al Pastor at El Rey del Taco
foodie.description: This no-sign cash-only spot in Villeray runs a vertical spit that produces the best al pastor in Montreal, full stop.
foodie.bonus: Order five tacos, eat them standing at the counter, and tip in cash.

foodie.title: Sunday Brunch at L'Express
foodie.description: The zinc bar, the tightly packed tables, and the steak tartare at noon make this Saint-Denis bistro feel like the best version of Paris that actually exists.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the bar alone, order in French start to finish, and strike up a real conversation with the bartender.

foodie.title: Croissant Morning at Automne Boulangerie
foodie.description: The laminated croissants here have a shatter-and-pull that puts most Parisian versions to shame, and the Saint-Henri lineup moves fast.
foodie.bonus: Get there before 9am, buy two croissants, eat one standing on the sidewalk immediately.

foodie.title: Tasting Menu at Au Pied de Cochon
foodie.description: Martin Picard's Plateau temple to foie gras, duck fat, and unapologetic excess is the most distinctly Montréalais meal you can sit down to.
foodie.bonus: Order the PDC poutine AND the foie gras cromesquis in the same sitting — no regrets, no sharing.

foodie.title: Pho Breakfast at Pho Tay Ho
foodie.description: This no-frills Villeray spot has been serving enormous bowls of bone-broth pho since before brunch was a concept, and the 8am crowd of regulars proves it.
foodie.bonus: Order the largest size and finish it entirely before anyone at your table does.

foodie.title: Lunch Counter at Wilensky's Light Lunch
foodie.description: This Mile End institution has been grilling the same Special — salami and bologna on a pressed roll — since 1932, and the mustard is not optional.
foodie.bonus: Order without looking at the menu and eat at the counter without checking your phone once.

foodie.title: Dinner at Joe Beef
foodie.description: The Little Burgundy institution that invented the modern Montreal dining scene still serves the most unapologetically indulgent plate in the city.
foodie.bonus: Order without looking at the menu — tell the server your mood and let them decide.

foodie.title: Bagel Taste-Test: St-Viateur vs. Fairmount
foodie.description: Pick up a wood-fired sesame bagel from each legendary Mile End bakery and settle the city's oldest food debate.
foodie.bonus: Vote out loud for a winner and defend your pick.

foodie.title: Smoked Meat at Schwartz's Deli
foodie.description: Squeeze into a communal table at the 1928 deli that put Montreal smoked meat on the map.
foodie.bonus: Order it 'fat' instead of your usual lean.

foodie.title: Sunday Morning at Jean-Talon Market
foodie.description: Fill a tote bag at one of North America's largest open-air markets, stall to stall with local cheese and produce.
foodie.bonus: Talk to one farmer about how they grew what you're buying.

foodie.title: Late-Night Poutine at La Banquise
foodie.description: Join the 2 a.m. lineup for one of thirty poutine varieties at Montreal's most iconic late-night diner.
foodie.bonus: Order the weirdest topping combo on the menu.
